data.narrative:
Fabri operates in Robotics & Manufacturing, a sector represented by a modest comp universe of nine peers: one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. The target's stage and current valuation remain undisclosed, limiting precision in peer selection.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. A review of ten same-sector peers identified zero companies at Fabri's undisclosed stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero within a comparable valuation tier. This filtering failure leaves insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to establish a reliable median multiple. Falling back to an all-sector median would introduce material noise and obscure meaningful comparables, rendering the method uninformative for triangulation.

No alternative methods could be applied with the available data. The absence of disclosed financials for Fabri (revenue, EBITDA, growth rate) precludes revenue or earnings multiple approaches. Without transaction data or disclosed round economics, precedent transaction and discounted cash flow analyses are similarly infeasible. The valuation framework cannot be completed from this dataset. A defensible range would require either: narrowing stage/tier filters to yield three or more true peers, obtaining Fabri's financial metrics, or accessing recent round documentation. Until such information surfaces, quantitative valuation synthesis is not warranted.
